message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties Involved | Main Causes |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East‑West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Doctrinal differences (e.g., the Filioque clause), ecclesiastical authority, cultural and linguistic divides, and political tensions between the Byzantine Empire and the Papacy. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Various Protestant movements (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, etc.) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Corruption and abuses in the Catholic Church (e.g., indulgences), theological disputes (e.g., justification by faith), the rise of vernacular scripture, and the political power of emerging nation‑states. |
| 3 | **East‑West Schism (also known as the Schism of 1054)** | 1054 CE | Same as #1 – the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches | (See #1) |

> **Note:** The Great Schism and the East‑West Schism refer to the same event; it is often listed twice in historical summaries because it is sometimes treated as a distinct “schism” in its own right and also as part of the broader East‑West divide. The Protestant Reformation is the third major split, leading to the creation of numerous Protestant denominations and fundamentally reshaping Western Christianity.
